name: Instrument — service rows with directly relevant project proof
borrow: a service promise and learn-more route beside two relevant project thumbnails with concise case summaries
why: Visitors encounter evidence for the exact offer they are evaluating, instead of having to infer relevance from a separate logo wall.
fit: A studio with a few clearly differentiated service families and two strong projects for each.
avoid: A new business without relevant work, or a large catalog whose offers require functional comparison rather than repeated editorial rows.
slots: Service name; outcome promise; detail route; two project visuals; client names; short project summaries; case-study destinations.
composition: A deep purple section introduces each service in a generous horizontal row. The left column uses a large serif name, short sans promise and pale pill action; the right has two rounded landscape thumbnails with names and descriptions below.
mobile_behavior: The service heading, promise and action precede a vertical sequence of project cards. Project captions remain below imagery and a visible View Case Study action appears in the saved phone view.
rebuild: Store each service with its promise, detail destination and selected project records. Use a weighted two-region desktop grid with a two-column proof subgrid. Stack service content before proofs on phones. Keep thumbnail, title and action tied to the same destination without duplicate confusing tab stops.
assets: Use two actual client project posters per service, with consistent crop ratios and color treatment. Supply real project summaries and destinations. Prepare static posters before adding video; source project media is study material.
adapt: Name services in customer language and make the promise distinct. Show only projects that demonstrate that capability. Reduce repetition if several services share the same two projects, and keep any qualification or scope details on the linked service page.
interaction: Service rows and project destinations inspected. The service-detail and case-study routes were not opened from these cards; no hover or media playback behavior was validated.

name: Humaan — six capability groups in a quiet type-led matrix
borrow: six clearly titled capability lists arranged in a three-by-two matrix without decorative card chrome
why: A concise grouping lets a buyer verify coverage across strategy, delivery and support without scanning repetitive marketing paragraphs.
fit: An established provider with a broad, concrete capability set that buyers need to check.
avoid: A primary offer that needs differentiation or persuasion; the matrix is supporting scope, not a complete service pitch.
slots: Capability introduction; six meaningful group names; short capability labels; relevant next route elsewhere on the page.
composition: Six evenly spaced groups sit on a pale blue field in three columns and two rows. Bold dark headings and left-aligned text lists supply hierarchy. Generous gutters and row spacing keep the dense inventory calm.
mobile_behavior: The groups become one vertical column, preserving their reading order. The phone view shows the first two complete groups and the start of the third. The source bottom navigation overlaps lower content at times.
rebuild: Model groups and items as semantic heading/list pairs. Use a three-column grid with consistent group gaps; collapse to one column when labels wrap awkwardly. Keep actual list text selectable and avoid individual cards unless the items need navigation.
assets: A considered type system and accurate capability inventory suffice. This pattern requires no decorative stock or generated imagery.
adapt: Use buyer-recognizable group labels, prune overlapping items and distinguish ongoing support from initial delivery. Pair the matrix with a concise offer and proof. Provide a nearby inquiry or service-detail route and keep sticky UI clear of content.
interaction: Static capability groups and responsive reflow inspected. No list interaction exists in the observed matrix; expertise navigation and inquiry routes were not exercised. Initial captures affected by the page's scroll animation were replaced.

name: ustwo — engagement offers with activities, outcomes and proof
borrow: an outcome-led service module with engagement timing, representative clients, explicit activities, outcomes and a relevant quote
why: The buyer can understand why to engage, what the work involves and what they should receive in one coherent module.
fit: A considered consulting engagement whose scope and outputs materially affect purchase decisions.
avoid: A quick commodity service or an offer with insufficient evidence to support lengthy scope and proof.
slots: Engagement phase; indicative duration; buyer goal; relevant client marks; short explanation; activities; expected artifacts/outcomes; attributed quote.
composition: A restrained white module divides a large goal statement and client marks on the left from explanation and paired activities/outcomes lists on the right. Phase and duration sit above. A large italic testimonial with an orange quotation mark follows.
mobile_behavior: The module becomes phase/duration, goal, marks, explanation, activities, then outcomes in one column. The supporting quote follows with attribution before the next offer begins; complementary phone views capture both portions.
rebuild: Create a repeated engagement module with scope and outcome fields separated in the data. Use a two-column desktop layout, then a small internal list grid. Stack in logical reading order on phones. Keep duration as a qualified expectation, not an unexplained guarantee.
assets: Approved client marks, a relevant attributed quote and a precise engagement definition. Typography and spacing carry the visual design; no large hero image is necessary.
adapt: Express the service as the customer's goal. Make activities concrete and outputs useful enough to inform a buying decision. Replace generic outcome promises with deliverables or success criteria that the team can actually commit to.
interaction: Services navigation and cookie dismissal were used. Scope lists, proof links and responsive order inspected; linked client stories, inquiry submission and any sales qualification flow were not tested.

name: Instrument — filterable work grid with separate display modes

why: Visitors can narrow work by capability and choose a browsing density while keeping project identity clear.

avoid: A small portfolio where filters hide scarce evidence or categories overlap so much that the selection adds little value.
slots: Portfolio introduction; category controls; current selection; display control; project poster; client/project name; category tags; project destination.
composition: A large brand heading precedes a thin rule and controls, with filters left and display mode right. In grid mode, two equally sized rounded image blocks sit in each row, with short client names and uppercase category labels below.
mobile_behavior: Grid cards become one column. The filter area condenses to a Filter control plus the selected category and a small Grid control. Project images keep generous size and names remain below them.
rebuild: Separate category and display state. Use real links with URL state when filtered pages are addressable; preserve category when changing display. Render project cards from one dataset and reserve image aspect ratios. Provide a meaningful no-results state and selected-control semantics.

adapt: Choose categories customers can use to assess relevance. Add a one-line project result if client names alone are insufficient. Reduce the source's large control-to-grid gap for a compact homepage version.
interaction: Grid mode was opened from the display control, then the product category selected; the resulting route retained /grid and the product chip was visibly selected. Phone controls were inspected but not opened. Several Vimeo embeds in stack mode were unavailable; grid posters loaded.

name: Humaan — featured project followed by paired visual cards
borrow: one wide flagship project leading into paired portrait-like project cards, with captions moved below images on phones
why: A clear visual priority gives the flagship room while the following pairs demonstrate breadth without identical repetitive tiles.
fit: A curated portfolio with one strong lead project and enough distinctive finished work to support varied crops.
avoid: An exhaustive archive where consistent compact scanning matters more than curation, or imagery too weak to carry large cards.
slots: Short work promise; sector/category routes; flagship poster; subsequent project posters; persistent project names; case-study destinations.
composition: On a warm light background, a nearly full-width rounded flagship card is followed by two large rounded cards per row. Website mockups and photography are composed as project-specific posters. Names sit at the bottom-left of desktop imagery.
mobile_behavior: Category routes wrap as pills. All projects become one column; the first project's name sits outside the image below, improving readability at small size. Floating bottom navigation can overlap the next card.
rebuild: Use a two-column grid with an explicit featured item spanning both columns. Define project-specific desktop and phone crops; move captions into normal flow at the mobile breakpoint. Keep each card a clearly named link with focus treatment independent of image motion.
assets: High-quality finished-work posters combining actual product views, brand graphics or photography. Prepare alternate crops and sufficient contrast behind desktop captions. Avoid manufacturing client work or implying unperformed projects.
adapt: Choose the flagship based on relevance to the buyer, not just visual spectacle. Add discipline or outcome captions where project names lack context. Keep captions visible on touch devices and position persistent navigation away from them.
interaction: Category destinations and project links inspected; category navigation, hover previews and project detail pages were not exercised. Featured remained the active route; the bright Education chip in the phone capture is a pointer-hover treatment.

name: Locomotive — project index with expandable rich previews
borrow: a scannable name/industry/location index that expands one project into imagery, scope and clear case-study/live-site routes
why: The compact list supports comparison, while optional rich previews let visitors inspect relevant work without leaving the index.
fit: A larger project archive whose industries and geography meaningfully help visitors select work.
avoid: A short portfolio that would be better shown immediately or a gallery where hidden imagery adds unnecessary friction.
slots: Portfolio promise; project count/filter; project name; industry; location; expand/collapse; preview image; scope; summary; year; case-study and live-site destinations.

name: Instrument / Oura — rationale, paired deliverables and a time-bounded impact block
borrow: a case-study sequence that connects design rationale to paired product/site visuals and a concise post-launch impact list
why: The sequence gives the viewer a reason for the design choices, concrete work to inspect and a clearly time-bounded result claim.
fit: A substantial redesign with documented research, finished artifacts and credible post-launch evidence.
avoid: A project with attractive mockups but no support for its claimed outcomes, or a case where a simple before/after image is sufficient.
slots: Client and challenge; design rationale; implementation principles; paired deliverable visuals; impact time window; result measures; attributed client proof; project roles.
composition: The case uses a dark slate field with light editorial prose in a narrower centered column. Two tall rounded visual panels show the product treatment beside its mobile website context. A later full-width impact heading and large bullet list state results with a post-launch window.
mobile_behavior: The impact heading and large result bullets become a single readable column. The saved phone frame includes the following media container, which failed to load in this environment. Desktop stills provide the usable visual evidence.
rebuild: Build the story from distinct context, decision, artifact and impact modules. Alternate reading-width text with wider media pairs. Store result value, unit, definition, period and evidence separately from visual styling. Stack media on phones and use explicit static posters if video cannot play.
assets: Client-owned finished product/site images, original rationale and verified analytics with permission to publish. Prepare paired crops that explain the relationship between product and experience, plus video posters and accessible descriptions.
adapt: Use only the client's actual results. Specify baseline, metric definition and observation period; the source's mobile-performance percentage is ambiguous and should not be copied as a complete measurement. Distinguish correlation from demonstrated causal impact.
interaction: Rationale, paired visuals, impact text and project roles inspected. No video was played, and some embedded media was unavailable. The results are source-reported claims, not independently verified conversion evidence.

name: ustwo / RVO Health — contextualized impact cards before the deeper story
borrow: an early impact section with three comparable result cards, each keeping its baseline or timeframe next to the headline figure
why: Readers can assess the project stakes and reported change before committing to the longer challenge and approach narrative.
fit: A product or service case with a few comparable, well-defined outcomes and a deeper explanation available below.
avoid: Results without denominators, baseline or timeframe, or an engagement story being misrepresented as a validated clinical outcome.
slots: Project identity and deliverable image; plain-language purpose; impact intro/timeframe; three result cards; comparison context; explanation; attributed proof; challenge; partnership; approach; next steps.
composition: A large product illustration introduces the case. The later dark impact band uses a centered reading-width heading/introduction, a wider row of three navy cards, then supporting prose. Bright figure labels and larger explanatory text separate the measure from its context.
mobile_behavior: The three impact cards stack in a single column with their comparison text intact. The explanatory narrative follows. The source uses very small condensed metric labels even on desktop; increase their size in an adaptation.
rebuild: Use a case-study article with separate context, impact, challenge and approach sections. Render impact cards from value/unit/baseline/period/evidence records. Set a shared desktop card grid and one-column phone layout; use actual text rather than embedding metrics into images.
assets: A real product poster with approved sample content, permissioned customer quote and documented measurement definitions. Protect user data in product captures; use synthetic examples for sensitive content while keeping the actual product design faithful.
adapt: Retain comparison and timeframe beside each number. Treat engagement measures as engagement, and specify the actual outcome being claimed. Review any clinical or regulated assertion with the evidence owner. Update dated future-tense rollout language rather than copying it.
interaction: The case was opened through the studio's work card. Context, impact cards and the challenge/approach structure were inspected. Video and inquiry routes were not exercised. Reported results and rollout claims were not independently verified.

name: Lime / TOKEN2049 — project facts, before/after evidence and an explained experiment
borrow: a concise scope table and visual A/B comparison connected to a result explanation that includes timeframe and sample sizes
why: The narrative makes the project accountable: visitors can understand the brief, inspect what changed and see the basis of the reported result.
fit: A design engagement with real strategic tradeoffs, visible deliverables and publishable comparison evidence.
avoid: Uncontrolled projects presented as experiments, or a case with no permission to show the previous design or its performance data.
slots: Project identity; brief; duration/status; category; scope; attributed customer proof; strategic decision and tradeoff; approach; before/after artifact; result method; lasting operational outcome; inquiry route.
composition: The white overview uses a serif heading, short context paragraph and thin ruled fact rows with labels left and values right. Dark green proof and visual regions interrupt the narrative. A large side-by-side A/B checkout image provides visual evidence; a later outcome section explains the comparison before the final inquiry band.
mobile_behavior: Overview facts become label/value stacks within ruled rows. Outcome prose becomes a narrow reading column with the reported timeframe and comparison counts kept together. Complementary phone views capture brief and results separately.
rebuild: Create a reusable case schema for context, project facts, decisions, artifacts and evidence. Use a definition list for project facts, reading-width narrative sections and a dedicated comparison figure with captions. Keep outcome method next to its claimed result; let phones open or zoom dense comparison artwork.
assets: Approved project artifacts, permission to show earlier/new designs, an actual experiment summary and an attributed quote. Provide legible individual comparison images for phones instead of relying solely on a dense combined screenshot.
adapt: Explain what the team chose and what it gave up. Report dates, sample sizes and outcome definitions when available. Only claim statistical significance when the client can supply the analysis; the source's test and uplift are reported, not independently audited here.
interaction: Overview, strategy, approach, comparison artwork and outcome explanation inspected. No checkout, booking or experiment was executed. The screenshot's image alt describes an older partnership-page visual, while the observed artwork is an A/B checkout comparison; the recipe follows the observed image.
